finding.claim: The named-pipe client connects to a deterministically named pipe without verifying the server process, so a local process that creates the pipe first receives agent requests and can return forged responses.
finding.source: Pipe name is derived from the username and CryptProtectMemory(CROSS_PROCESS) of 'Pageant', which any local process can compute (namedpipes.rs:49-52). Precondition: real Pageant absent or raced.
finding.sink: ClientOptions::new().open(&pipe_name) at namedpipes.rs:33; the stream then carries list-identities and sign requests.
finding.guards_checked: No GetNamedPipeServerProcessId, owner, path or session check. CryptProtectMemory errors are discarded (namedpipes.rs:110-114), so the name falls back to a plain hash. The name is not a secret. Response/request correlation is not checked.

finding.claim: FindWindowW locates the agent by class and title only, so a same-session window named 'Pageant' receives WM_COPYDATA containing the shared-memory name and can read requests and return forged responses.
finding.source: Any same-session process that creates a window with class and title 'Pageant' and wins enumeration order, or runs while Pageant is absent.
finding.sink: SendMessageA(WM_COPYDATA) at wmmessage.rs:217-224, with the shared-memory name in the payload at wmmessage.rs:209-215.

trace.note: query_pageant_direct run in a spawned task
SendMessageA blocks until the target window returns
response read from the same mapping, unvalidated

finding.guards_checked: No check of owning PID or image path. No request/response correlation. UIPI may limit some cross-integrity cases; not verified. A hostile window can block SendMessageA indefinitely, hanging a runtime worker.

finding.claim: The reader buffers up to a 4 GiB length-prefixed message before checking it against _AGENT_MAX_MSGLEN, so attacker-supplied bytes can exhaust client memory.
finding.source: Bytes written to the PageantStream. In agent-forwarding setups these may come from a remote SSH server; this depends on the calling stack, which is not in this repo.
finding.sink: BytesMut growth at interface.rs:36 and the wait for len+4 bytes at interface.rs:44.

trace.note: read_buf drains the duplex without limit
len read from u32 prefix, up to 4 GiB
continues until len+4 bytes buffered, no cap

finding.guards_checked: _AGENT_MAX_MSGLEN (interface.rs:195) is applied only after buffering. The duplex has no backpressure because the reader drains unconditionally. On 32-bit Windows, len+4 can wrap at interface.rs:44 and 47.

finding.claim: MapViewOfFile's result is not checked for null, so a failed mapping leads to a null-pointer write in MemoryMap::write.
finding.source: MapViewOfFile failure under resource exhaustion. Not attacker-controlled.
finding.guards_checked: pos+len > length bound at wmmessage.rs:140 guards length only, not the pointer.

finding.claim: MemoryMap::read writes into a Vec through out.as_ptr() as *mut u8, which is undefined behaviour because the Vec is not mutable and as_ptr is documented read-only.
finding.source: Any call to MemoryMap::read. Not attacker-controlled.

trace.note: out.as_ptr() cast to *mut u8 and written through

finding.guards_checked: Length bound at wmmessage.rs:161 is correct. The issue is only the mutability of the write path.

finding.claim: Stripping the '@domain' suffix from the username can make different users map to the same pipe name, producing a connect failure or a misdirected connection.
finding.source: Two users with the same SAM name in different domains, or a UPN containing '@'.

trace.note: pipe name built from the truncated name

finding.guards_checked: The pipe DACL probably prevents cross-user access, so the likely effect is DoS rather than disclosure. Not verified.
